paths.formulation: P = \{\text{simple paths } (v_0, \dots, v_r) \text{ in } (N, E) : v_0 \in N_S,\; v_r \in N_B\}

pE.formulation: pE_{p,i,j} = 1 \iff (i, j) \text{ is an edge of path } p

code.python: pE = [[[1 if (i, j) in set(zip(path, path[1:])) else 0 for j in range(nN)] for i in range(nN)] for path in paths]

pRank.formulation: pRank_{p,v} = \text{position of } v \text{ along path } p\text{, and } 0 \text{ if } v \notin p

code.python: pRank = [[path.index(v) if v in path else 0 for v in range(nN)] for path in paths]
pCost = [[sum(tc[i][j][k] for i, j in zip(path, path[1:])) for k in range(nK)] for path in paths]

cE.formulation: cE_{c,i,j} = 1 \iff (i, j) \text{ is an edge of cycle } c

code.python: cE = [[[1 if (i, j) in set(cycle) else 0 for j in range(nN)] for i in range(nN)] for cycle in cycles]
cCost = [[sum(tc[i][j][k] for i, j in cycle) for k in range(nK)] for cycle in cycles]
e = [[1 if path[-1] == j else 0 for path in paths] for j in B]

notes: Formulation `a` ships over the arcs of the supply network $(N, E)$; formulation `b` ships along whole supplier-to-camp routes, so the map enumerates the network's simple paths and derives $nP$, $pE$, $pRank$, $pCost$, and $e$ from them.

The shared graph assumptions (no arcs entering suppliers and no arcs leaving camps) ensure that the unfiltered path and cycle enumeration produces exactly the structurally admissible routes and cycles.

Since `a` admits cyclic flows, the map also enumerates the network's simple directed cycles and derives $nC$, $cE$, and $cCost$; these carry the cost of the circulating component that no path variable can express.
